items.title: 'Not a single minister present': Hassan Karim calls out empty benches
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A government backbencher today expressed disappointment over the absence of ministers in the Dewan Rakyat as he prepared to speak during the policy-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027. Hassan Abdul Karim (PH-Pasir Gudang) said he wanted to support Budget 2027, which he believed contained several positive measures, but was disappointed that no minister was present to hear his views. The policy-stage debate on Budget 2027 is scheduled to run until Oct 22, following its tabling by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 9.

items.title: PM Anwar expresses concern over Middle East conflict, condemns Houthi attacks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia continues to view with great concern the dangerous escalation of conflict unfolding across the Middle East, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said that he has been in close contact with key regional leaders, including Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed Salman and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed Abdulrahman Al Thani. He emphasised that this same moral conviction compels Malaysia to speak out with equal firmness whenever innocent civilians are targeted anywhere else.

items.title: MRT Corp and TNB explore green rail solutions, to start with RTS Link
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) and Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) will explore renewable energy, energy efficiency and electrical reliability solutions for rail infrastructure. The two organisations will assess opportunities to integrate renewable energy, improve energy efficiency and strengthen electrical infrastructure reliability. The agreement outlines three areas of collaboration, including solar energy solutions, electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure and electrical reliability and maintenance services.

items.title: Tuition teacher charged with sexual offences against three 11-year-old pupils
items.summary: news@nst.com.my KUALA LUMPUR: A tuition teacher was charged in two Sessions Courts here today with six offences involving sexual assault and unnatural sex against three 11-year-old boys. Four charges alleged that the primary school teacher, who also ran tuition classes, had sexually assaulted the three pupils at a house in Kampung Muhibbah, Jalan Puchong, between July and September. He was charged under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which provides for a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.

items.title: Malaysian Bar, office-bearers awarded RM59,499 after winning part of appeal over 2022 independence march
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 21 —The Court of Appeal today partly allowed the Malaysian Bar’s appeal over its 2022 Walk for Judicial Independence, awarding RM59,499 in damages to the Bar and four of its office-bearers for violating their constitutional rights in connection with the march. The march was held on June 17, 2022, to protest the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) public announcement of an investigation into then Court of Appeal judge Datuk Mohd Nazlan Mohd Ghazali, now a Federal Court judge. On March 20 last year, the Kuala Lumpur High Court held that the police had acted ultra vires (beyond their powers) by imposing conditions prohibiting the march, but awarded the Bar only RM1 in nominal damages, a sum proposed by the Bar’s counsel.

items.title: Greek students, teachers, civil servants plan cost of living protests
items.summary: ATHENS: Students, teachers and civil servants will rally in Greece on Wednesday to protest against the high cost of living, saying they face the same problems that sparked violent demonstrations in France at the weekend. Gatherings are expected around midday (0900 GMT) in Athens and Thessaloniki, the country's second-largest city. "In Greece like in France, we are demanding public, free education," Katia Koubousidou, head of a student union at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, told AFP.

items.title: Court to decide on former judges' pension suit on Jan 28
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here has fixed Jan 28 next year to deliver its decision on a suit filed by a group of 19 people, comprising former members of the judiciary and widows of former judges, against the government and three others over the alleged failure to provide an appropriate increase in their pensions and benefits since 2015. Previously, 36 people, comprising former members of the judiciary and widows of former judges, were named as plaintiffs in the suit filed in Jan 2022. However, 17 people have been removed as plaintiffs from the suit, including former Chief Judges of Malaya Tan Sri Siti Norma Yaakob, who died in March this year, and Tan Sri Haidar Mohamed Nor, as well as former Court of Appeal judge Tan Sri Mohamad Ariff Md Yusof, who is also a former Dewan Rakyat speaker.

items.title: Video of Kuching international school student's penknife attack goes viral
items.summary: KUCHING: A video of an international school student's penknife attack this morning, which left a teacher injured, has gone viral on social media. Some social media accounts claimed the 16-year-old had livestreamed the attack on an online community platform before the video was deleted. Sarawak acting police commissioner Deputy Commissioner Saifullizan Ishak confirmed the incident.

items.title: Civil servant held over RM30mil bribes linked to RM140mil tax assessments
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A civil servant suspected of soliciting and accepting about RM30 million in bribes to help several companies reduce tax assessments totalling RM140 million was arrested at a hotel in the Klang Valley early today. He was brought before the Putrajaya Magistrate's Court this morning, where magistrate Ezrene Zakariah granted a six-day remand order until Oct 26. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Gentari, BYD Malaysia explore flash charging rollout
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Gentari Sdn Bhd and BYD Malaysia Sdn Bhd are exploring the deployment of BYD Flash Charging technology as the country's electric vehicle (EV) market continues to expand. The partnership will also explore opportunities in renewable energy generation and energy storage, combining Gentari's clean energy expertise with BYD's energy storage and technology capabilities. He said BYD's expertise in EVs, batteries and high-power charging technology, combined with Gentari's experience in developing and operating charging networks, will provide a foundation for strengthening Malaysia's EV charging ecosystem.

items.title: 'As a grandfather, I feel their pain': Zahid mourns five-year-old Asiah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he was deeply moved by the death of 5-year-old Asiah Ahmad Syahir in a six-vehicle crash on Jalan Kuching, particularly as he has grandchildren of the same age. Zahid, who visited the girl's family in Kampung Sungai Penchala earlier today, said it was heartbreaking to see a young life cut short. Zahid expressed his condolences and prayed for the family to remain strong.

items.title: JP Morgan sees Bank Negara rate hike in Q1 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to raise the overnight policy rate (OPR) by 25 basis points (bps) in the first quarter of 2027, according to JP Morgan. The US investment bank said it expects Bank Negara to keep the benchmark rate unchanged at its upcoming November policy meeting before raising it by 25bps in Q1 2027. On inflation, JP Morgan kept its headline and core consumer price index (CPI) forecasts at 1.8 per cent and 1.9 per cent respectively for this year, with both gauges stepping down to 1.7 per cent next year.

items.title: Johari: Malaysia’s chip talent retention remains sustainable despite foreign offers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Starting salaries for junior engineers and technicians in the local chip industry scale up steadily with experience, offering sustainable career progression even as overseas markets tempt local talent with higher pay, said Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today. Johari acknowledged the salaries may seem nominally low when compared to what companies in countries like Taiwan or South Korea may offer, but said they must still weigh higher overseas pay against the increased cost of living in those countries. “If compared with job offers overseas in places like the UK, Singapore, Korea, or Taiwan, salaries might be two to three times higher,” Johari said during Question Time.

items.title: Sultan of Pahang warns youths against social ills, culture of hatred
items.summary: PEKAN: The Sultan of Pahang has expressed concern over worsening social ills among youths, including drug abuse, bullying, online gambling and inappropriate relationships. Be brave enough to disagree, but never lose your sense of judgement," he said in his speech at the proclamation ceremony for Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah's (UMPSA) Tuanku Chancellor Hall here today. Also present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir, Pahang Education Committee chairman Datuk Seri Ir Mohd Soffi Abd Razak and UMPSA Pro-Chancellor Tan Sri Abi Musa Asa'ari Mohamed Nor.

items.title: Akmal to auction motorcycle, tilapia to pay RM300,000 to Teresa Kok
items.summary: In a Facebook post, he said he had decided to sell the two assets after realising his savings were insufficient to cover the amount ordered by the court. Akmal said he respected the court's decision and was prepared to take responsibility for paying the RM300,000. Akmal said parting with the two assets would be difficult because they held sentimental value for him.

items.title: Penang named Southeast Asia's only city on National Geographic's 2027 travel list
items.summary: State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the list, unveiled yesterday, featured 25 destinations and travel experiences recommended for travellers next year. Wong said Penang's selection followed a nomination, research and reporting process involving National Geographic's travel experts and Nat Geo Traveler's international editorial teams. "Being featured once again by National Geographic further reinforces Penang's appeal as an international tourism destination.

items.title: For Lula, Brazil's sovereignty is at stake in final election
items.summary: "Brazil does not fit into anyone's backyard," he said, in a veiled dig at US President Donald Trump's administration, which he believes is challenging Brazil's sovereignty. In the candidates' first debate days before the vote, Lula accused the Bolsonaro family, headed by former President Jair Bolsonaro, of being "subordinate to American interests," pointing to May meetings between the Bolsonaros and Trump earlier this year before Trump imposed new tariffs on Brazilian products. The election's first round showed the limits to Lula's message.

items.title: Nancy: Counselling for victims of AI-generated nude images
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry is offering counselling to victims of AI-generated nude images and their families following a case involving female students in Negri Sembilan. She said the ministry had counsellors through its agencies, including the Social Welfare Department and the National Population and Family Development Board, who could assist victims and their families. On Oct 18, media reports said more than 300 female secondary school students in Seremban, Negri Sembilan, were believed to have been victims of AI-powered image manipulation to create nude images.

items.title: Perhilitan action in Chemor prompts elephants to move away
items.summary: IPOH: The Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) has driven wild elephants away from Bukit Bangkong, Chemor, following repeated incursions into orchards. In a statement, Perhilitan said it received complaints about elephant disturbances on Sept 27, Oct 3 and Oct 11. The department began monitoring the area on Oct 4 before carrying out control measures on the nights of Oct 11 and 12.

items.title: Loke envisions Transport Expo Asia rivalling LIMA as regional mobility showcase
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke hopes the biennial Transport Expo Asia (TXA) will develop into a premier international showcase on par with the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA), drawing top global exhibitors and industry investors to Malaysia. Loke said that the event serves as an ideal launchpad to spotlight progress across land transport, aviation, maritime, and logistics sectors, placing particular emphasis on emerging technologies like autonomous driving, robotics, and unmanned aerial systems. “We certainly hope this will help drive growth in the transport sector through greater strategic cooperation,” he said.

items.title: #NSTViral: Police hunt Porsche driver over road bullying in Bandar Kinrara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracking down the driver of a black Porsche Cayenne caught on dashcam footage driving recklessly, chasing another motorist and attempting to force the vehicle to stop in Bandar Kinrara. Hasbullah said initial investigations found that the incident occurred around 2.15pm on Oct 18 along a three-lane road near Bandar Kinrara 3. "The driver then accelerated, prompting the Porsche driver to give chase," he said.

items.title: Complex chip development can cost up to US$300 million
items.summary: He said the government's collaboration with global technology company ARM provided access to technology but did not cover the full cost of chip development. "Even a simple chip costs about US$50 million, while a complex chip can cost up to US$300 million," he said in the Dewan Rakyat. Johari said the collaboration with ARM, signed in 2025, provides two types of tokens — Compute Subsystem (CSS) and ARM Flexible Access (AFA) — to help local companies develop integrated circuit chip designs.

items.title: Australian lawmaker loses both legs, knew family of suspected attacker
items.summary: MELBOURNE: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has had both legs removed, her husband told journalists on Wednesday, after what police called a "targeted" attack. Police have charged 43-year-old Brendan Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison. Nugent has been charged with dangerous driving, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a federal public official.

items.title: Two hikers swept away by strong currents at Batang Kali waterfall
items.summary: BATANG KALI: A search and rescue operation is underway for two hikers swept away by strong currents while swimming at Lubuk Tupai Waterfall in Kampung Hulu Rening. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received a distress call at 12.13pm. Ashrul said rescue personnel faced difficulties reaching the waterfall due to its remote location.

items.title: Sarawak completes integrated rare earth elements roadmap to build ‘super magnet’ industry, says Awang Tengah
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — The Sarawak government has completed an integrated framework for the development of the rare earth elements (REE) industry, covering the entire value chain from upstream to downstream activities, said Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan. The Second Natural Resources and Urban Development Minister said the Sarawak REE Industry Development Roadmap aims to develop a ‘super magnet’ industry to support the growth of Sarawak’s semiconductor, aerospace, and satellite industries, in addition to applications in electric vehicle manufacturing, defence technology, medicine, and other sectors. On a related matter, Awang Tengah said the Sarawak Minerals Management Authority (SMMA) has approved the Sarawak Mineral Industry Development Policy, which comprises seven pillars and 43 key components.

items.title: Injured teacher rushed to hospital after wresting penknife from student
items.summary: In a notice to parents, guardians, staff and students, the school said the incident was isolated and no other injuries were reported. Police arrived shortly after and contacted the student's parents. The school said the student had not approached other students and that no students were in danger throughout the incident.

items.title: Teacher injured while disarming student in Kuching school
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — A teacher was injured while attempting to wrest a sharp object from a student at an international school here this morning. It is learned that the secondary school student was brought under control and taken to the principal’s office before the police arrived and took over the matter. Kuching district police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu, when contacted, said the police are looking into the incident.

items.title: Malaysia condemns Houthi attacks, stresses safe passage through Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has condemned Houthi attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia continued to view with great concern the escalation of conflict unfolding across the Middle East. Anwar cited the recent attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which he said killed civilians, including pilgrims.

items.title: Agent charged with harbouring 7 undocumented migrants, possessing 6 passports
items.summary: PASIR MAS: An agent was charged at the Sessions Court here today with harbouring seven undocumented migrants and possessing six passports belonging to other people without lawful authority in Tumpat on Oct 14. The charge was framed under Section 55E(1) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. He was charged under Section 12(1)(f) of the Passport Act 1966.

items.title: Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centres popular
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that companies building data centres should pay a "dividend" to the communities where they are sited if they want to make the developments popular. "I have watched the process closely, and data centres that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck," Trump said in a Truth Social post. Trump said in February that major technology companies must build their own power plants for their data centres in order to protect consumers from rising bills.

items.title: Timeline: Pas and Bersatu in Perlis political crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Political turmoil in Perlis has resurfaced following Bersatu's decision to suspend Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah. Mid-Dec 2025: Five Bersatu and three Pas assemblymen reportedly withdraw support for Menteri Besar Mohd Shukri Ramli. Dec 28, 2025: Bersatu's Abu Bakar Hamzah is sworn in as the new Menteri Besar.

items.title: KLIA deploys K9 sniffer dog units to tighten airport security and curb smuggling
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 21 — Trained sniffer dog units will begin patrolling passenger terminals and restricted baggage zones across KL International Airport (KLIA) from Oct 26, Malaysia Airports announced today. The airport operator described the deployment as a multi-layered security strategy that shields public passenger-facing concourses while reinforcing back-of-house operations alongside existing surveillance architecture. Malaysia Airports managing director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said integrating canine units into daily operations strengthens inter-agency vigilance to safeguard international travellers, visitors, and airport staff, while freeing airport Aviation Security (AVSEC) teams to concentrate on their primary protective functions.

items.title: Man charged with raping 15-year-old girl in Rompin
items.summary: KUANTAN: A 20-year-old man claimed trial at the Sessions Court here today to raping a 15-year-old girl in a hotel in Rompin in June. Deputy public prosecutor Fatin Nadirah Kasim prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyer Mohd Fadzli Mohd Ramly. Sazlina set bail at RM5,000 with one surety.

items.title: North Korea says 'new firepower units' in place after border threat
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korea has moved new units into "firing positions", the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un said Wednesday, days after Pyongyang warned it was considering deploying additional strike means to its border with South Korea. "Our military leadership underlined the need to make those rogues aware that our new firepower units have taken their firing positions," Kim Yo Jong said, according to state media. Her statement came a day after Seoul warned of a "firm" response to further North Korean provocations.

items.title: Lecturer loses RM270,000 to phone scam, duped into handing over ATM card
items.summary: KUANTAN: A lecturer lost RM269,993 after falling victim to a phone scam in which she was tricked into surrendering her bank card and pawning her jewellery. "She was threatened with an arrest warrant, the freezing of her bank accounts and imprisonment before being instructed to surrender her automated teller machine (ATM) card and make payments purportedly for bail," he said in a statement today. Her ATM card remains in the suspects' possession," he said.

items.title: NCT Alliance earns Selangor industrial park recognition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: NCT Alliance Bhd has received the Preferred Industrial Park (PIP) certificate from Invest Selangor, recognising its role in supporting the state's industrial development through its flagship NCT Smart Industrial Park (NSIP). NCT Alliance said the recognition reinforces its commitment to developing quality industrial parks and attracting high-impact investments to Selangor. At SIBS 2026, NCT Alliance also showcased its second industrial park development, NCT Innosphere (NIS).

items.title: Penang schools to operate as usual on Thursday despite haze
items.summary: The Penang Education Department said it would continue monitoring air quality and prioritise the safety, health and well-being of students and education personnel. "We remain concerned about the safety and health of students amid the deteriorating air quality," it said in a statement. The department said students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precaution and drink sufficient water to stay hydrated.

items.title: No more ‘kindergarten colours’: DBKL opts for neutral tones in RM446m public housing facelift
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The capital’s public housing schemes are receiving a major aesthetic and safety facelift, with City Hall (DBKL) foregoing garish paint schemes for neutral tones while overhauling critical electrical infrastructure across dozens of ageing buildings. Speaking during a working visit to People’s Housing Programme (PPR) Taman Mulia in Bandar Tun Razak today, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said that DBKL made a deliberate shift away from the bright, multi-coloured exteriors long associated with government flats. At PPR Taman Mulia, DBKL committed RM6.67 million in restorative works for roughly 2,128 residents.

items.title: Malaysians who lend MyKad to foreigners face up to three years’ jail, says Home Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Individuals who misuse their identity cards (MyKad) by ‘renting out’ or handing them over to foreign nationals could face up to three years in prison, a fine of up to RM20,000, or both, Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said. He said the National Registration Regulations 1990 provide strict legal measures to curb foreign nationals’ misuse of national identity. Shamsul Anuar said the operation underscored the importance of joint enforcement efforts by the National Registration Department (NRD), the Immigration Department and Labour Department.

items.title: Find another way: Civil servants effectively banned from using Waze app due to Israel ties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Civil servants have been banned from using the Waze navigation app with immediate effect, following a decision by the National Cyber Security Committee (JKSN) at its meeting yesterday. In a letter dated October 20, Chief Secretary to the Government (KSN) Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said the JKSN Meeting No. 3 of 2026 was chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

items.title: Ten former Negri exco members seek Federal Court interpretation of ruler’s powers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 21 — Ten former Negeri Sembilan state executive council (exco) members have filed an application in the Federal Court seeking to challenge the state ruler’s decision last month to revoke their appointments. The 10 are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Datuk Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah. They named the Negeri Sembilan state secretary and the state government as respondents.

items.title: Businessman charged with cheating Datuk Seri out of over RM10m in AMLA probe scam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — A businessman was charged at the Sessions Court here today with four counts of cheating another businessman, who holds the title Datuk Seri, by claiming he could help resolve issues involving frozen bank accounts and a police investigation into more than RM10 million. The deception allegedly induced Keh to hand over cash amounting to RM2 million, RM3 million, SGD1.5 million and RM500,000 to Tan through Datuk Seri Chiau Beng Teik, in which Keh would not have handed over the money had he not been deceived. “If the court allows bail, the prosecution proposes RM2 million.

items.title: Hadi: PAS, aligned Perikatan parties to take joint action over RoS notice
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — PAS will join aligned Perikatan Nasional (PN) component parties in challenging a notice to cancel the coalition’s registration in court and preparing for the Melaka state election. PAS said the decision appeared to pre-empt a court ruling and restrict democratic rights guaranteed under the Federal Constitution. It said relations among PN’s component parties remained strong, except for one party which it claimed had distanced itself from the coalition and turned away.

items.title: Toll concessionaire ALR clears RM2.1b in debt, eyes early highway handover to Putrajaya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Amanat Lebuhraya Rakyat Berhad (ALR) has crossed the RM2 billion threshold in cumulative sukuk principal and profit repayments, positioning the private not-for-profit firm to return four major Klang Valley toll highways to the government by 2033, five years ahead of schedule. “On October 13, 2026, ALR made its eight sukuk payment of RM513.8 million comprising RM390 million to Sukuk Principal and RM123.8 million to Sukuk Profit, bringing its cumulative Sukuk Principal and Profit payments to more than RM2.149 billion. “The Sustainability Sukuk Murabahah Programme carries total sukuk principal and profit obligations of RM7.935 billion,” ALR group chief executive officer Muhammad Nizam Alias told a media briefing at the SMART headquarters here today.

items.title: Sabah commercial vehicle body vows action against operator after deadly Sepanggar Port accident
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 21 — The Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (CVLB) Sabah will take action against the operator of the trailer truck involved in the fatal accident near Sepanggar Port on Sunday. Chairman Datuk Phoong Jin Zhe said the board will meet on Oct 30 to discuss and finalise appropriate action against the operator. The container then fell onto a passing car.

items.title: High Court stays Malaysian Bar’s challenge against Zahid’s DNAA pending apex court appeal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The High Court has granted an interim stay on the Malaysian Bar’s judicial review challenging the Attorney General’s decision to halt corruption proceedings against Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. The decision freezes the challenge until the Federal Court disposes of the government’s appeal. The freeze halts High Court proceedings after the Federal Court recently granted both the AG and the deputy prime minister leave to challenge an earlier Court of Appeal verdict that had permitted the Malaysian Bar to pursue its judicial review.

items.title: Can the Yamtuan remove excos without MB’s advice? Sacked Negeri Sembilan councillors turn to apex court
items.summary: The lawsuit challenges the decision by Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir to revoke their appointments, an order that took effect on Sept 20 and was formally gazetted on Sept 24. The applicants comprise former councillors Faizal Ramli, Zaifulbahri Idris, Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umairah Hashim, Asna Amin, Razi Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Fairuz Isa, and Razali Abu Samah, FMT reported. The application names the Negeri Sembilan state secretary and the state government as the first and second respondents respectively.

items.title: Telcos set for bigger say as DNB ownership transition nears
items.summary: The transition follows DNB’s completion of a RM5.2 billion financing exercise, paving the way for the Ministry of Finance Inc (MOF Inc) to exit as an ordinary shareholder. CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL are expected to hold equal stakes in DNB, while MOF Inc will retain a special share covering key strategic matters. However, he said it remained unclear whether the change would translate into any immediate shift in DNB’s technology suppliers.

items.title: Rapid KL trials fixed-schedule feeder vans in Cheras and Putrajaya, ditching app bookings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Commuters in parts of Cheras and Putrajaya will soon be able to board feeder vans on fixed timetables without booking via an app, as Rapid KL kicks off a three-month pilot project this Saturday, to boost first- and last-mile connectivity. The trial shifts two existing Rapid KL On-Demand (ROD) zones, routes T400B and T512B, away from dynamic ride-hailing to predetermined routes and schedules. Route T400B bridges Bandar Tun Razak and Taman Midah, creating a direct ground link between the LRT Sri Petaling Line at Bandar Tun Razak station and the MRT Kajang Line at Taman Midah station.

items.title: Loke: Prasarana open payment system procurement to be finalised by year-end
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Prasarana Malaysia Berhad is in the final stages of procuring a new open payment system that will allow commuters in the Klang Valley and Penang to pay for rail and bus fares using debit and credit cards, mobile wallets, and QR codes, Transport Minister Anthony Loke told Parliament today. The initiative was first announced in 2023, and Loke at the time said a new payment system was needed to modernise fare collection across public transport networks operated by Rapid Rail and Rapid Bus by integrating more payment methods alongside existing options. Loke said the new system will also support QR code ticketing, QR-based payments, Touch ‘n Go cards, and other future approved payment mediums.

items.title: No order to step down: Shuhaily to remain on duty after claiming trial to assaulting Special Branch cops
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysian Checkpoints and Borders Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain will remain at his post and carry out his duties as normal unless directed otherwise by the government, his legal team confirmed today. Speaking to reporters outside the Sepang Sessions and Magistrates’ Court Complex, lawyer Datuk Rosal Azimin Ahmad said no official instructions or interdictions have been issued by administrative authorities barring his client from continuing as a senior civil servant. Rosal clarified that any formal determination regarding Shuhaily’s service status rests entirely in the hands of the Public Service Department and central government leadership, Berita Harian reported.

items.title: ‘If not us, who?’ — Nga Kor Ming hits back at critics of PM’s support for local artists
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming has defended Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over his attendance at pop idol Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza's traditional concert last weekend, saying such patronage was vital to Malaysia’s creative industry. Nga rejected criticisms over Anwar's presence at the weekend performance, stressing that government leadership must champion homegrown talent if the nation hopes to build a thriving arts ecosystem. “So I want to ask: if the prime minister doesn't support local artists, then who will?

items.title: Floodwaters destroy Pos Brooke suspension bridge, leaving villagers isolated
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 21 — A flash flood, accompanied by surging waters and a mudflow, caused the Kampung Brooke Lama suspension bridge across Sungai Belatop in Pos Brooke here to collapse yesterday afternoon. Kampung Brooke Lama headman Rian Bujang said rain began at about 4 pm before the flash flood struck at around 5.30pm, sending strong currents crashing into the bridge, causing it to collapse and its concrete pillars to break. He said the bridge, built in 2008, served as an access route to Sekolah Kebangsaan Pos Brooke and Pos Brooke Health Clinic.

items.title: Perlis MB Abu Bakar stripped of party posts after Bersatu issues two-term suspension
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) has suspended Perlis Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah for two terms, effective Oct 13. Perlis Bersatu state chairman Izizam Ibrahim confirmed the punitive action today, acknowledging that the formal notification letter was served on Abu Bakar last week after an internal disciplinary inquiry, Berita Harian reported. The letter, dated Oct 14, 2026, was signed by Bersatu disciplinary board chairman Datuk Mohd Radzi Manan.

items.title: Closing pig farms could weaken food security, says LDP leader
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 21 — Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) vice-president David Ong has criticised a proposal to shut down pig farms nationwide and rely on imported pork, saying it could undermine Malaysia’s food security, local agriculture and multicultural values. Ong was responding to a suggestion by Tasek Gelugor MP Wan Saiful Wan Jan, arguing that environmental and public health concerns should be addressed through better farm management, modern technology and stricter environmental standards rather than closing the industry. Ong said policies must also respect Malaysia’s diverse communities and dietary practices, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, while balancing environmental protection with agricultural development.

items.title: MCBA chief Shuhaily charged with assaulting Special Branch duo at KLIA
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysian Checkpoints and Borders Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain was charged at the Magistrate's Court here today to two counts of assaulting police personnel at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) last month. Shuhaily claimed trial after both charges were read before Magistrate Khairatul Animah Jelani, FMT reported He is accused of two counts under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt to Lance Corporal Faiz Saman and Lance Corporal Ekmal Sofwan at KLIA Terminal 1 on Sept 28. Khairatul allowed Shuhaily bail of RM3,000 with two sureties across both charges, and fixed Nov 25 for case management.

items.title: Guan Eng warns of SME liquidity crisis over RM30b delayed tax refunds
items.summary: Lim, who is the member of parliament for Bagan, pointed to the 2025 Federal Government Financial Statements, which show that outstanding tax refund liabilities decreased by RM3.425 billion, dropping from RM33.342 billion in 2024 to RM29.919 billion in 2025. To curb systemic delays, Lim proposed placing a strict RM10 billion cap on federal tax refund arrears. Outstanding tax refund commitments stood at RM21.836 billion in 2021, before climbing to RM25.721 billion in 2022 and RM25.511 billion in 2023.

items.title: Perak Perhilitan monitoring elephant herd after crop destruction complaints
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 21 — The Perak Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) has received six official complaints this year from oil palm smallholders in Kampung Perlop 1, Sungai Siput, over wild elephants destroying crops and plantation infrastructure. Its director, Dr Pazil Abdul Patah, said the herd is estimated at between three and eight elephants, believed to have come from the nearby Korbu Forest Reserve. "Perhilitan also believes these are the same elephants that encroached into fruit orchards around Bukit Bangkong, Chemor, on Oct 15, as both locations fall within the range of the Korbu Forest Reserve," he said in a statement.

items.title: Corporate-creative collaborations vital to boost Malaysian IPs, says Teo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Collaborations between corporate entities and local creative talent are vital in driving the growth of Malaysia’s creative sector and showcasing homegrown intellectual properties (IPs) to a broader audience. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said such strategic collaborations between corporate entities and homegrown creative teams allow local artists, animators, performers, and production personnel to showcase their skills on a wider stage. That connection helps our creative industry and our tourism industry grow together,” Teo said.

items.title: Malaysia calls for WHO-led pooled medicine purchasing amid supply risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia has proposed that the World Health Organisation (WHO) Western Pacific Region (WPRO) urgently pilot a pooled procurement project for selected medicines to ensure drug security in the region. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the move was urgent as almost the entire region is facing critical challenges due to disrupted supply chains, market uncertainty, and high reliance on Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) imports, with international geopolitical conflicts worsening the situation. He said the pooled procurement pilot project must involve selected medicines with healthy supplier competition and clear shared needs, and must be implemented transparently.
